paper_sections.title: Estimating effective connectivity in Alzheimer's disease progression: A dynamic causal modeling study

description.value: The study estimated resting-state effective connectivity among regions of the default mode, salience, and central executive networks across cognitively normal, early MCI, late MCI, and Alzheimer's disease groups, and tested group differences and associations with MMSE and CDR scores.

design.value: A longitudinal ADNI-2 resting-state fMRI study of four clinically defined subject groups whose progression stages remained stable throughout data collection visits spanning at least 24 months; dynamic causal modeling with PEB and Bayesian Model Reduction was used to estimate effective connectivity, followed by ANOVA and linear regression.

task_description.value: Resting-state functional images were obtained using an echo-planar imaging sequence. During the fMRI scans, all participants were instructed to keep their eyes open and relax.

description.value: Resting-state functional images were obtained using an echo-planar imaging sequence. Each series has 140 volumes, and each volume consists of 48 slices of image matrices with dimensions 64 × 64.
T1 image used for unified segmentation to the Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) space.

The first 10 volumes of each functional time series were discarded from analysis. The remaining 130 volumes were corrected for the staggered order of slice acquisition. The preprocessing also included regression of head motion parameters, realignment for head movement, and spatial normalization using T1 image unified segmentation to the Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) space.

steps.value: The first 10 volumes of each functional time series were discarded from analysis
Correction for the staggered order of slice acquisition
Spatial normalization using T1 image unified segmentation to the Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) space

model_settings.value: The regions of interest were modeled as nodes in effective-connectivity networks. The neuronal model included intrinsic connectivity, extrinsic connectivity, input, and state noise; the observation model was a generalized BOLD signal model. Seven ROIs were used: mPFC, bilateral PCC, bilateral dlPFC, and bilateral ACC.

estimator.value: Parametric empirical Bayes (PEB), Bayesian Model Reduction (BMR), and thresholding by likelihood/free energy evidence

model_settings.value: Connectivity strengths for each subject group were compared; Bonferroni correction was applied for multiple comparisons.

Forward step-wise linear regression was used for MMSE; both forward and backward connections between L-dlPFC and mPFC were predictive of CDR. Effective connectivity between brain regions was tested as a predictor of cognitive scores.

estimator.value: forward step-wise linear regression; forward and backward regression
